comments: F/imm briefly on river then north
Regular count at this time of year now.
Bird first found yesterday 1st/2nd year male.
Foraging in riffled areas immediately downstream of small dams
2CY male photographed, present for second day
one individual seen in grassy area close to sand dune
one individual seen in grassy area close to sand dune
At least 200 on sea by musselburgh lagoons
One male hunting in the grass near the dunes
One adult sitting proud on hawthorn bush
Non full adult male - white cheek and tail barred but upperparts dark grey
5 adults and 4 juveniles in a mixed Tern roost.
Known 2cy male. Very active and hunting not to far away from everyone watching.
Juvenile on bushes nearby to the Red-footed Falcon.
Very kindly pointed out to me by another birder :)!!
Smaller than surrounding Sandwich terns, black bills with seemingly red legs and long tail streamers. PTBU.
Known bird seen at dunes and surrounding area, excellent views! PTBU.
Juvenile with stonechats near sand spit where Red-footed Falcon was.
Bird that has been present for past 24h
Flock on the water off sea wall
1st summer individual seen on sand dunes
flying around and feeding around dunes
Black cap, scaly back pattern, and broad white inner edge to the wings seem to lead to it being a juvenile roseate tern.
Red footed falcon photographed hunting. Was sighted yesterday at same location, so came to see it myself.

Went back for a second look at the 1st Summer mRFF. It hovered regularly, and swooped low over the grassland catching insects. As the wind strengthened it sought shelter in the lee of bushes, and spent time on the ground. It was quite hobby like in the air, but looked longer tailed, especially when in hover mode. Some excellent images have been posted on facebook.
Adult and two juveniles. One of the juveniles decided to perch about 2 metres away from me at one point! I don't think I will ever get this close to one ever again!
Two males and one female type amongst Scoter flock for most of the day
Found a single bird showing characteristics of this species/sub species
Some lovely full adult summer birds within flock of around a dozen birds
2 adult drakes with velvet scoter flock on sea
At least a couple hundreds on sea

Seen circling over Threipmuir reservoir. Several times it flew off down Green Cleugh and returned some time later from the ENE, presumably having done a loop by Loganlea/Glencourse reservoirs.
Saw it dive and catch a fish, and fly off to the west with it while being harassed by gulls.
Juvenile or dark morph far out to sea. Briefly chased a Tern or Kittiwake.
In an a feeding flock with other seabirds.

Adult, seen close (with Redshank and a Ruff), all relevant features seen: small size compared with Redshank/ Ruff, white rump with faint dark barring at tip, short whitish supercilium (not very obvious) etc.
Male near the sand dunes. Would perch on posts in the area.
Known bird. Male, long winged, dark grey, with bright orange-red feet and undertail. Seen well perching, hovering, foraging.
One amongst the velvet scoter flock
Perched and hovering over the dunes. Long winged falcon with red-orange eye ring, bill, and legs. Barred underwings. Grey back. Photos added.
Distant Large flock by sea wall
With velvets seen briefly being elusive
A big raft on the sea
1m - white and orange bill / head seen well
Bright red thick bill, darker head and no black on wing tips plus white non joined up white eyering
Be cautious as you approach as not to scare bird
